meta.title: The Locked Bunkhouse
meta.unit: Of Mice and Men — dreams, loneliness, friendship
meta.subject: English: Language & Literature
meta.author: ISH English

story.intro: You are locked inside the bunkhouse. George's worn notebook holds the way out. Solve each clue to lift the final latch before the others return.
story.outro: The latch lifts. You step into the cool night, the dream of a little place still glowing. You read the story's heart and earned your way out.

stations.name: The Coded Cover
stations.narrative: George's notebook is locked. Four words sit on the cover in a simple code.
hints: Each letter has shifted forward in the alphabet.
Shift every letter back by 3 (D becomes A).
P→M, L→I, F→C, H→E… read it out.
stations.reveal: Correct — 'Mice and Men'. Steinbeck took his title from a Robert Burns poem about plans going wrong.

stations.name: Crooks's Word
stations.narrative: A brass plate names the word that guards the next door.

content.definition: Set apart or alone; kept away from others.
content.sentence: Forced to sleep apart, Crooks lived an ____ life.

hints: The sentence says he sleeps apart from everyone.
It describes being kept away from others.
It means set apart — it begins with 'i'.
stations.reveal: Yes — 'isolated' means set apart or alone. Crooks is isolated by racism as well as distance.

stations.name: The Order of Things
stations.narrative: Four moments have scattered. Lay them in order to free the next bolt.

content.prompt: Put these events in the order they happen.
items: George and Lennie reach the ranch
Lennie kills Curley's wife in the barn
George shoots Lennie by the river

stations.answer: George and Lennie reach the ranch|Lennie is given a puppy|Lennie kills Curley's wife in the barn|George shoots Lennie by the river
acceptedAnswers: George and Lennie reach the ranch|Lennie is given a puppy|Lennie kills Curley's wife in the barn|George shoots Lennie by the river
hints: Begin where the two men start the novel.
The gentle moment with the puppy comes before the barn.
Arrival, puppy, the barn, the river.
stations.reveal: Right order. Steinbeck moves us steadily from hope to heartbreak.

stations.name: The Gatekeeper's Question
stations.narrative: The heavy door asks a careful reader one question.

content.passage: George and Lennie share a dream of a little place of their own, with rabbits and a patch of land. On the lonely ranch, the dream is the one warm thing they carry between them.
content.question: In the novel, the dream of 'a little place of our own' mainly represents…
options: hope and belonging in a lonely world

stations.answer: hope and belonging in a lonely world
acceptedAnswers: hope and belonging in a lonely world
hints: Think about why the dream comforts them when times are hard.
It is about more than land — it is about not being alone.
Choose the option about hope and belonging.
stations.reveal: Yes — the dream stands for the hope and belonging the ranch's lonely men long for.

stations.name: The Final Latch
stations.narrative: One word, spelled true, lifts the last latch.

content.definition: The deep sadness of being without companions — a central theme of the novel.
content.hintLetters: l _ n _ l _ n _ s s

hints: It is the feeling shared by Candy, Crooks and Curley's wife.
stations.reveal: LONELINESS — the ache at the centre of the book. The latch lifts. You are free.
